metadata.title: Results from TALIS 2024: Flemish Community of Belgium

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 note reports results for lower secondary teachers and principals based on the TALIS 2024 Database. The note does not describe the microdata extraction steps or the specific sampling/replicate weight variables used in the underlying TALIS analyses, so weight application cannot be verified from the text provided. The reported percentages and statistically significant differences are therefore best interpreted as survey-weighted estimates produced by OECD using TALIS’s complex survey design (school- and teacher-level sampling). For any re-analysis, analysts should use the official TALIS 2024 sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the TALIS database documentation to obtain correct standard errors and significance tests.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This note is a descriptive results brief based on TALIS self-reports (teachers’ and principals’ perceptions and practices) rather than an achievement assessment with plausible values. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the outcomes summarized here. The note also does not report a specific missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or exclusion rules), which is typical for high-level OECD results briefs that rely on internal TALIS processing documented elsewhere.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note presents findings for the Flemish Community of Belgium based on TALIS 2024 responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals. It comments only on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average, but it does not specify additional analytic filters (e.g., exclusions, response-rate thresholds, or sub-sample restrictions) in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 results note summarizes teacher and principal self-reports for the Flemish Community of Belgium, focusing on lower secondary education and comparing estimates to the OECD average-27. The brief reports descriptive indicators (e.g., teacher age and gender composition, experience, perceived ability to adapt teaching to diversity, social and emotional learning support, technology/AI use, professional learning opportunities, instructional autonomy, collaboration patterns, well-being and job satisfaction, and intentions to leave). It also highlights only statistically significant differences or changes, and it cautions that some estimates may be affected by non-response bias. Because TALIS is based on self-reports, cross-country comparisons should be interpreted cautiously as perceptions can be shaped by social and cultural context. The note does not provide model-based ML results, performance metrics, or an explicit causal identification strategy.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD TALIS 2024 results brief rather than an empirical ML study: it does not train or evaluate predictive models, and it does not report an analytic sample size or per-country counts in the provided text. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, plausible-value handling, missing-data handling, and structured predictive findings are either not applicable or not reported in this document excerpt. The extraction is therefore limited to the descriptive TALIS indicators and their comparisons to the OECD average as presented.
